texts.orig: To produce a nanostructured metal foam; we ignite pressed pellets of high-nitrogen metal com- plexes in an inert atmosphere at different pressures . As a rapidly burns, its volume dramatically increases; the burning complex releases heated metal atoms, which attract each other and coalesce into larger particles. At the same time, decompo sition such as hydrogen and nitrogen, also released by the reaction, blow tiny holes through the coalescing metal to form nanoscopic pores. The resulting foams typically contain 50% to 70% metal, with the remainder carbon nitride-type impurities that can be removed later by heat treatment. pellet gases being Possible applications for our nanostructured metal foams abound, including catalysis, fuel cells, and hydrogen storage.
